description: Scikit-learn-compatible feature selection: the Relief family (ReliefF, SURF, MultiSURF, TuRF), mRMR, JMI, CMIM, FCBF, MIFS, CIFE, DISR, CFS, MDR, Chi2, Gini index, Laplacian Score and mutual-information estimators, accelerated with Numba on CPU, NVIDIA CUDA and Apple Silicon (Metal) GPUs.
rules: Install with `pip install fast-select`; add the `[metal]` extra (`pip install "fast-select[metal]"`) for the Apple Silicon GPU backend.
Every estimator takes `backend`: 'auto' (CUDA, then Metal where enabled, then CPU), 'cpu', 'gpu' (CUDA only) or 'metal'. Explicit 'gpu' or 'metal' raises if unavailable instead of falling back.
For Relief-family estimators, an integer `n_features_to_select` is a count and a float is a fraction of features.

JMI, CMIM, FCBF, MIFS, CIFE, DISR and mRMR expect categorical (discrete) features and do not bin continuous data; discretize continuous features first, or use `mutual_info_classif` / `mutual_info_regression` with `SelectKBest`.
`mutual_info_classif` and `mutual_info_regression` match the scikit-learn signatures and return nats; set `random_state` for reproducible results.
When migrating from scikit-rebate, rename `categorical_threshold` to `discrete_limit` and note that the default `n_neighbors` is 3 (scikit-rebate uses 100).
